notes: Scope: all five packet elements are produced by the servo_state_publisher executable (CMakeLists.txt:98-103, src/servo_state_publisher.cpp); references are limited to what that node consumes. Topic name is written relative as "joint_states" on the default NodeHandle nh() (line 108, 162); it resolves to /joint_states in the root namespace, recorded verbatim in declares. Publishing is event-driven from the rc_out callback (no rate set); queue size 10. QoS is null because this is ROS 1. definition_id is null for every port, and the msg:sensor_msgs/JointState hash and the three field types (header.stamp, name, position) are in neither declares nor not_declared: the sensor_msgs and std_msgs definitions are not in the snapshot, and ros_distro is null, so there is no release tag from which the protocol permits fetching them (the snapshot's .travis.yml sets ROS_DISTRO=hydro for CI, but no dependency tag was inferred from it and nothing was fetched). Units are null: position is a linear map of the normalised PWM into the URDF joint's <limit> lower/upper (lines 99, 154-155), so it inherits URDF limit units, but the code does not state them (defaults -M_PI/4..M_PI/4 at lines 37-38 are only used by the unused default constructor). The node also reads its own private parameters ~<joint>/rc_channel, rc_min, rc_max, rc_trim, rc_dz, rc_rev (lines 130-142) whose joint names come from the parameter dictionary at run time; these are not packet elements. header.stamp is never assigned (only name and position are filled, lines 195-196); velocity and effort are also left empty. The rc_out subscriber topic is hard-coded as "rc_out" (mavros's RC plugin advertises "out" under its rc namespace, mavros/src/plugins/rc_io.cpp:43), so a remap is expected at launch; no launch file in the snapshot starts servo_state_publisher.
